skill.name: chapter-outline-generator
skill.description: Generates comprehensive chapter outlines for books, including key topics, subtopics, learning objectives, and estimated word counts. Use this when the user needs help structuring a book chapter or creating a table of contents.
skill.summary: Creates structured chapter outlines with summaries, learning objectives, sections, subsections, and estimated word counts.
skill.author: AbdulSamad94

content.value_statement: Planning chapters is difficult when ideas lack order and proportion. This skill turns a book concept into structured chapter plans with sections, objectives, and word counts.
actual_capabilities: Collects book title, genre, audience, theme, length, and desired chapter count.
Creates chapter titles, summaries, learning objectives, sections, and subsections.
Estimates word counts for chapters based on book length and chapter importance.
Checks chapter order for logical flow, topic gaps, and balanced coverage.
Formats the result as a clear hierarchical outline for fiction or nonfiction projects.
limitations: Does not write the full manuscript or complete chapter prose.
Requires user context to produce accurate structure and priorities.
Word count estimates are planning aids and need author review.
Does not verify facts, citations, market fit, or publishing requirements.

use_cases.title: Plan a First Draft
use_cases.description: Turn a book idea into a chapter-by-chapter structure before drafting begins.

use_cases.title: Organize Expert Knowledge
use_cases.description: Convert a professional framework into nonfiction chapters with objectives and sections.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Outline
use_cases.description: Review chapter balance, topic flow, and missing sections in a draft outline.

prompt_templates.title: Outline a New Book
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a complete starting outline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a chapter outline for a book titled [title]. The genre is [genre], the audience is [audience], and the main theme is [theme]. Aim for [word count] words and [chapter count] chapters.

prompt_templates.title: Expand One Chapter
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for deeper chapter planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Expand chapter [number] of my book into a detailed outline. Include a summary, learning objectives, main sections, subsections, and an estimated word count.

prompt_templates.title: Rebalance a Table of Contents
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this table of contents and suggest a stronger chapter order. Identify gaps, overlaps, uneven chapter lengths, and sections that need clearer objectives.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Part Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with constraints across a full manuscript.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-part book outline for [subject]. Use [number] parts, [chapter count] chapters, clear progression, chapter objectives, subsections, and word count targets for each chapter.

output_examples.input: A mystery novel about a detective investigating art thefts, with the first three chapters planned.
output_examples.output: A three-chapter opening arc with chapter titles, case setup, suspect introductions, scene sections, and estimated chapter lengths.

output_examples.input: A nonfiction book about remote team management for new managers.
output_examples.output: A structured business book outline covering remote work context, leadership principles, communication systems, and measurable chapter objectives.

output_examples.input: A rough table of contents that feels repetitive and uneven.
output_examples.output: A revised chapter order with merged topics, clearer section boundaries, missing topics, and adjusted word count targets.

best_practices: Provide the audience, book purpose, and desired length before asking for an outline.
Review the full outline for flow before drafting individual chapters.
Adjust word counts after confirming which chapters carry the main argument or plot.
anti_patterns: Requesting a full outline with no audience, theme, or genre information.
Treating estimated word counts as final publishing requirements.
Using the first outline without checking for gaps, repetition, or pacing problems.

faq.question: Can this skill outline fiction and nonfiction books?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports fiction, nonfiction, educational, business, and general book structures.

faq.question: Does it write the full chapter text?
faq.answer: No. It creates planning outlines with summaries, objectives, sections, subsections, and estimated word counts.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the title, subject, audience, main theme, target length, and preferred chapter count when available.

faq.question: Can it fix an existing outline?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review order, balance, gaps, overlap, and chapter purpose in an existing outline.

faq.question: Are the word counts exact?
faq.answer: No. They are planning estimates based on the requested book length and chapter importance.

faq.question: Does it check factual accuracy?
faq.answer: No. Authors must verify facts, citations, claims, and subject-specific requirements separately.
